The memory directory is denied by permission settings, so I'll skip saving the note. The policy is finished and verified, so here is the summary.

**Result:** `policy.py` completes 113/113 notes on the six training charts, every hit judged "perfect" (timing error 0 ± 2 ms), with `plan()` averaging under 1 ms. A backup of this version is in `history/policy_v1_100pct.py`.

**Strategy**

- **Perception** (calibrated with `probe.py` against ground truth, hit-time error 1.4 ms std): colour-segment the frame into cyan taps, green holds, magenta slides. A head is a 38 px bar in a lane column; its bottom row gives the hit time (335.18 − 206.26·t). A hold's body column top gives its end time. Slides are connected components; the body is traced upward row by row from each head, following the nearest run, yielding a (time, lane) profile that is refreshed every frame, so parked heads and bodies still off-screen are handled.
- **Tracking**: detections are matched to tracks by kind, lane and hit time; hit estimates are averaged over frames, hold/slide ends are refined as bodies scroll in. Ghost heads from slide bend joints are rejected by requiring 7 clean rows and a blank row below.
- **Scheduling**: notes within 35 ms form chord groups. Each note gets several candidate hand poses: gripper closed on the lane, or opened 1, 2 or 2.6 lanes with either fingertip on the note, which cuts travel distance. Pairs up to 2 lanes apart become one two-finger press. A DP picks at most one pose per group to maximise notes completed under a calibrated transition model (lift overlapping lateral travel at 1.4 m/s, settle, descend, slow gripper width changes, ~0.23 s minimum re-tap cycle). The previous plan gets a stickiness bonus, and an action is committed at its arrival time so decisions never flip mid-descent.
- **Holds with taps**: a hold can be pressed with one fingertip while the other is rolled up (`rise`); taps in the free fingertip's lane are then played by rolling it down and back up. This was validated by an experiment (fake holds beside isolated taps, all taps perfect) since the training charts contain no such pattern.
- **Execution**: keyframes start from the current commanded pose, hover height adapts to available time, slides are followed with a 60 ms look-ahead, and any exception falls back to a hover plan while resetting state.

**Caveats:** the hidden charts may contain patterns the training set lacks (crossing slides, taps during holds, very dense streams); the first two are handled by code paths that were only partially exercised here, and streams faster than ~0.23 s per same-lane note are deliberately thinned by the scheduler rather than attempted.

Still 113/113 on the training charts, with the new capability in place and backed up as `history/policy_v2_rock.py`.

**What I changed and why**

The training set was already at 100%, so this revision targets dense charts, where one fingertip's ~0.23 s press cycle forced the scheduler to thin fast note streams.

- **Rocking chains of taps.** Consecutive taps whose lanes match the two fingertips of a still hand (1 or 2 lanes apart) are now one action: the first tap lands with the hand rolled so only one fingertip touches, then each following tap is played by rolling onto the other fingertip. Each roll is a fresh touch, so spacing down to 0.16 s works, versus 0.23 s plus travel before. Chains extend greedily through consecutive single taps alternating lanes, and the DP weighs them against normal play at 0.95 value per tap.
- **Calibration by experiment.** I validated the mechanism with fake presses on the training charts before enabling it: at 0.14 s spacing the rolling fingertip landed late (several "great" judgments), so rocked touches are commanded 30 ms early and the minimum spacing is 0.16 s. With that, all rocked taps were "perfect" for both the one-lane and two-lane gaps.
- **Plan builder support.** Chain keyframes alternate the keyframe reference fingertip and the roll sign, and the release keyframe uses the last fingertip pressed.

Caveat: the training charts contain no fast alternating patterns, so the chain path is exercised in scoring only through the experiment runs above, not through the final clean evaluation.

Still 113/113 on the training charts, with the new version backed up as `history/policy_v3_samelane.py`.

**What I changed and why**

Training was already at 100%, so this revision again targets patterns the hidden charts are likely to have: fast repeated taps in the **same lane**. Until now those needed a full single-finger press cycle (about 0.23 s), and anything faster was thinned by the scheduler.

- **Same-lane rocking chains.** With the gripper nearly closed (38 mm tip gap) both fingertips sit inside one lane, so consecutive taps in that lane can be played by rocking between the fingertips, the same mechanism as the cross-lane chains from the last revision. Chain generation now iterates over three tip gaps: within one lane, one lane apart, two lanes apart.
- **Calibrated by experiment.** Fake rock presses on isolated training taps showed same-lane rocking completes every tap, but with a steeper roll it is less precise: at a 34 mm gap and 0.16 s spacing two touches were only "good", at 38 mm and 0.18 s one was. So same-lane chains require 0.18 s spacing and are valued at 0.85 per tap, which means the DP uses them only when normal single-finger play cannot fit the notes.
- **Minor cleanups**: chain geometry helper for lane distance, candidate generation restructured so chains no longer depend on the open-pose list.

Caveat: as before, the clean training run never triggers chains (no fast repeats in the training charts), so the chain code paths are verified only through the experiment runs, which exercise the same keyframe generation.

Still 113/113 on the training charts, backed up as `history/policy_v4_chainhold.py`.

**What I changed and why**

Training was already perfect, so this revision closes another gap that dense charts expose: a tap followed within ~0.23 s by a **hold** in the same lane or a neighbouring one. Previously that spacing was below the single-fingertip press cycle, so the scheduler had to drop either the tap or the hold.

- **Rocking chains may now end in a hold.** A chain of alternating-fingertip taps can terminate with a hold note: the hand rolls onto the hold's fingertip and keeps it pressed until the hold ends (release time extends to the hold's end). The action takes the hold's kind so its end keeps being refined from the image while it is played.
- **Validated by experiment** before enabling: isolated training holds were played as "fake tap on the other fingertip, then rock onto the hold". All of them completed with 100% contact and perfect hit timing.
- **Guard:** the rolled-hold logic that adds extra sub-taps during a hold is not applied to chain-terminal holds, since chains have their own keyframe path.

As with the previous revisions, the clean training run never needs chains, so the new path is exercised only through the experiment runs.

Still 113/113 on the training charts, backed up as `history/policy_v5_holdchain.py`.

**What I changed and why**

This round found and fixed a real bug in the chain code that none of the earlier clean runs could reveal, and added one more pattern.

- **Integration stress test.** I temporarily inflated the modelled descent time so the scheduler was forced to use rocking chains on the training charts' real notes. Chains of one-lane, two-lane and same-lane taps were chosen and every chained note registered, confirming the DP, commitment and keyframe paths work together, not just inside the fake-press experiments.
- **Bug fix: chains rolled too early.** Once a tap's dwell keyframe was in the past, the next plan interpolated from the current pose straight to the next rock keyframe, so the roll began immediately and slowly. This cost rocked holds half their contact (48%) and explained the occasional early same-lane touches. The plan now keeps the previous fingertip pressed until the roll is due, then rolls over the calibrated 74 ms. Rocked hold releases went from 48% to 98–100% contact.
- **Chains may now start with a hold.** A hold followed closely by a tap in the same or a neighbouring lane is played by rocking onto the other fingertip once at least 85% of the hold has elapsed (the judge needs 80%). Validated by experiment: all such holds completed with 98–100% contact. Holds whose end is still unknown (body off-screen) are excluded.
- **Rolled approaches get a minimum 0.15 s ramp** so the roll is established before touchdown; a conservative, cheap safeguard.
- **Experiment harness fix** (a string/float bug that only affected calibration runs, never the clean policy).

One same-lane rocked tap out of ~17 still lands "good" rather than "perfect"; it is completed, and same-lane chains are only used when a note would otherwise be lost.
